title: Lines, Shapes and Art Around the World
subject: arts

sections.body: Artists use LINE (straight, wavy, zigzag), SHAPE, COLOUR and TEXTURE (how something feels: rough, smooth, bumpy).
Art from around the world looks different: Aboriginal dot paintings from Australia, Madhubani art from India, Mexican papel picado paper banners.
When you look at art, say what you NOTICE: colours, shapes, how it makes you feel.
Draw a picture using only wavy lines, then one using only dots!
Look at art from your family's heritage together, and from a culture you don't know yet.

quiz.q: How something feels when you touch it (rough, smooth) is called…
hints: Think about touching sandpaper or silk.
Bumpy, fluffy, smooth: these all describe…?
quiz.explain: Texture is how something feels, or looks like it would feel.

quiz.q: Dot paintings are a famous art style from which place?
hints: Dot paintings come from a very old culture.
Madhubani art comes from India. Dot paintings come from…?
quiz.explain: Dot paintings are a famous Aboriginal Australian art style.

quiz.q: What kind of line is this? /\/\/\
hints: Look at the points. Are they sharp or round?
This line goes up and down with sharp corners.
This line ~~~ goes up and down smoothly. That is a wavy line. Is /\/\/\ smooth?
quiz.explain: It goes up and down with sharp points. That makes it a zigzag line!
